issues.legal_issue: Land acquisition proceedings are deemed to have lapsed when the award was made well before the 2013 Act and possession of the affected land was not taken.
material_facts: An award concerning the respondent's land had been passed in 1986.
The acquiring authority conceded that it had not taken possession of 1,100 square yards of the respondent's land.
The High Court declared the acquisition proceedings lapsed, and the acquiring authority appealed.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition proceedings in respect of the 1,100 square yards were deemed to have lapsed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 applies to the acquisition of land for which an award had been made well before that Act and possession had not been taken. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_lapse_declaration and land_acquisition_proceeding and award_preceded_new_act_by_five_years and possession_not_taken

predicates.appeal_challenges_lapse_declaration: The acquiring authority appealed against a declaration that the acquisition proceedings had lapsed.
predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns proceedings to acquire land.
predicates.award_preceded_new_act_by_five_years: An award for the land was made at least five years before the new land-acquisition law took effect.
predicates.possession_not_taken: The acquiring authority had not taken possession of the affected land.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a lapse declaration in land acquisition proceedings, and the award preceded the new law by at least five years while possession was not taken, the acquisition proceedings for the affected land are deemed lapsed.
